title: Alcachofas a la Plancha
shortDescription: Griddled baby artichokes, garlic, lemon, sea salt
note: Great with cold cava on a warm evening.
introCopy: Baby artichokes halved and seared hard on a hot griddle until the leaves crisp and the hearts turn tender and sweet.

steps.text: As you trim and halve each artichoke, drop it into a bowl of water with the lemon juice to keep it from browning.
Pat the artichokes dry. Heat 2 tbsp olive oil on a griddle or heavy skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear the artichokes cut-side down for 5-6 minutes until deeply browned, then flip and cook 3-4 more minutes until tender.
Add garlic in the last minute, then finish with remaining oil, parsley, and flaky salt. Serve with lemon halves.

title: Gildas
shortDescription: Skewered anchovy, olive, and guindilla pepper
note: The classic Basque pintxo — one bite, eaten in a single go.
introCopy: A tiny skewer stacking briny anchovy, a plump green olive, and a sharp pickled pepper — San Sebastián's most famous bar snack.

steps.text: Thread onto each small skewer, in order: a folded anchovy fillet, an olive, and a guindilla pepper folded in half.
Arrange on a plate and drizzle with a little olive oil just before serving.

title: Navajas a la Plancha
shortDescription: Griddled razor clams, garlic, olive oil, lemon
note: Serve the moment they come off the heat — razor clams toughen fast.
introCopy: Razor clams hit a screaming-hot pan for just a couple of minutes, finished with garlicky oil and a squeeze of lemon.

steps.text: Heat a griddle or wide skillet over high heat until smoking hot.
Lay the razor clams flat on the griddle and cook 1-2 minutes, just until they open and curl slightly.
Warm the olive oil with garlic in a small pan for 30 seconds until fragrant, then spoon over the clams.
Scatter with parsley and serve immediately with lemon wedges.

title: Almejas a la Marinera
shortDescription: Clams simmered in white wine, garlic, and paprika
note: Perfect with crusty bread for mopping up the broth.
introCopy: A classic seafood-shack tapa — clams steamed open in a garlicky white wine and paprika sauce.

steps.text: Heat olive oil in a wide pot over medium heat. Cook onion until soft, about 5 minutes, then add garlic and paprika for 1 minute.
Pour in the white wine and bring to a simmer.
Add the clams, cover, and cook 4-5 minutes, shaking occasionally, until they open. Discard any that stay closed.
Stir in parsley and serve straight from the pot with bread for the broth.

title: Ensalada de Naranja y Bacalao
shortDescription: Salt cod, orange, red onion, olives
note: A bright, no-cook classic from Andalusia and the Levante coast.
introCopy: Flaked salt cod tossed with juicy orange segments, shaved red onion, and briny olives — sweet, salty, and refreshing all at once.

steps.text: Arrange the orange segments on a platter and scatter the flaked cod over the top.
Layer the red onion and olives over the salad.
Drizzle generously with olive oil, finish with black pepper, and serve at room temperature.

title: Pimientos Rellenos de Atún
shortDescription: Piquillo peppers stuffed with tuna and roasted red pepper
note: Best served slightly chilled or at room temperature.
introCopy: Sweet roasted piquillo peppers filled with a creamy tuna mixture — a tapas-bar refrigerator staple.

steps.text: Mix the tuna, mayonnaise, diced roasted pepper, chives, salt, and pepper in a bowl until well combined.
Spoon or pipe the tuna mixture into each piquillo pepper.
Arrange on a platter and chill 15 minutes before serving, or serve right away.

title: Tomates Aliñados
shortDescription: Marinated tomatoes, sherry vinegar, garlic, cumin
note: Only worth making with tomatoes that are truly in season.
introCopy: Ripe tomatoes marinated in sherry vinegar, garlic, and a whisper of cumin — a simple bar-counter classic.

steps.text: Arrange tomato wedges on a platter and season lightly with salt.
Whisk together garlic, sherry vinegar, olive oil, and cumin.
Spoon the dressing over the tomatoes and let sit at room temperature 10 minutes before serving.

title: Judías Blancas con Almejas
shortDescription: White beans, clams, garlic, white wine
note: Hearty enough to share as a two-bite tapa or scale up for dinner.
introCopy: Creamy white beans and briny clams simmered together with garlic and a splash of white wine — coastal comfort in a small bowl.

steps.text: Heat olive oil in a wide pot over medium heat. Cook onion until soft, about 5 minutes, then add garlic for 1 minute.
Add the white beans and wine, and simmer 5 minutes to let the flavors meld.
Nestle in the clams, cover, and cook 4-5 minutes until they open. Discard any that stay closed.
Stir in parsley and serve warm in small bowls.

title: Espinacas con Garbanzos
shortDescription: Sevillian spinach and chickpeas, cumin, sherry vinegar
note: A tapas-bar staple across Seville, usually served warm in a small clay dish.
introCopy: Wilted spinach and tender chickpeas simmered with garlic, cumin, and a splash of sherry vinegar for tang.

steps.text: Fry the bread and garlic in 1 tbsp olive oil until golden, about 2 minutes, then blend or mash with cumin and paprika into a paste.
Heat remaining oil in a wide pan, wilt the spinach in batches, about 4 minutes.
Stir in the chickpeas and the garlic-bread paste, along with a splash of water, and simmer 5 minutes.
Finish with sherry vinegar and salt to taste, and serve warm.

title: Ensalada de Pulpo y Patata
shortDescription: Octopus and potato salad, paprika, olive oil
note: The tapas-bar cousin of pulpo a la gallega, served cool as a salad.
introCopy: Tender octopus and waxy potatoes tossed with smoked paprika and good olive oil — a Galician classic reworked as a shareable salad.

steps.text: Simmer the octopus in a large pot of water 35-40 minutes until fork-tender. Cool slightly and slice into rounds.
Meanwhile, boil the potatoes in salted water 12-15 minutes until tender, then drain.
Toss the octopus and potatoes with olive oil, smoked paprika, and salt.
Scatter with parsley and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Bacalao con Tomate
shortDescription: Salt cod simmered in a rich tomato sauce
note: Sits well overnight — flavor deepens by the next day.
introCopy: Flaked salt cod simmered gently in a slow-cooked tomato and onion sauce, scented with bay and a touch of sugar.

steps.text: Heat olive oil in a wide pan and cook onion until soft, about 6 minutes. Add garlic for 1 minute.
Add crushed tomatoes, bay leaf, and sugar. Simmer uncovered 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened.
Nestle in the cod chunks and simmer gently 8-10 minutes until just cooked through.
Remove the bay leaf and serve warm with bread.

title: Coca de Verduras
shortDescription: Catalan flatbread topped with roasted peppers and onion
note: Cut into small squares for easy sharing.
introCopy: A thin, crisp Catalan flatbread piled with sweet roasted peppers and onions — the Mediterranean answer to pizza.

steps.text: Heat oven to 425°F. Toss peppers and onions with 2 tbsp olive oil and salt, spread on a tray, and roast 20 minutes until soft and lightly charred.
Stretch the dough thin on an oiled baking sheet.
Top the dough with the roasted vegetables and drizzle with remaining olive oil.
Bake 10-12 minutes until the crust is golden and crisp. Cool slightly, cut into squares, and serve.

subRecipes.title: Make your own pizza dough
steps: Whisk the flour, yeast, and salt together in a large bowl.
Add the olive oil and warm water, and mix until a shaggy dough forms.
Turn out onto a floured surface and knead for 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Place in an oiled bowl, cover, and let rise in a warm spot for 1 hour, until doubled in size.
Punch down and roll out to about 1 lb of dough, ready to use in place of store-bought pizza dough.

title: Alcachofas Confitadas
shortDescription: Artichokes slow-cooked in olive oil with garlic and thyme
note: Keeps well in the fridge for a few days, submerged in its oil.
introCopy: Artichoke hearts poached low and slow in olive oil until meltingly tender, perfumed with garlic and fresh thyme.

steps.text: Place artichoke hearts, garlic, and thyme in a small pot and pour in olive oil to submerge.
Warm over low heat, keeping the oil at a gentle simmer, until the artichokes are fork-tender, about 25 minutes.
Let cool slightly in the oil, then stir in lemon juice and salt to taste.
Serve warm or at room temperature, spooning a little of the infused oil over the top.

title: Ensaladilla de Marisco
shortDescription: Chilled potato salad with shrimp, peas, and light mayo
note: A lighter, seafood-forward take on the classic Spanish potato salad.
introCopy: Cool potatoes, sweet shrimp, and peas bound with a light mayonnaise dressing — a bar-counter staple served ice-cold.

steps.text: Boil the potatoes and carrot in salted water 12-15 minutes until tender, then drain and cool.
Combine potatoes, carrot, peas, and shrimp in a large bowl.
Fold in the mayonnaise gently and season with salt and pepper.
Chill at least 30 minutes before serving cold.

title: Boquerones a la Plancha
shortDescription: Griddled fresh anchovies, garlic, parsley, lemon
note: Not to be confused with the vinegar-cured version — these are cooked hot and fast.
introCopy: Fresh anchovies seared quickly on a hot griddle with garlic and lemon — crisp-edged and delicate inside.

steps.text: Heat a griddle or heavy skillet over high heat with half the olive oil.
Lay the anchovies flat and sear 1-2 minutes per side until just cooked through.
Scatter garlic over the fish in the final 30 seconds of cooking.
Finish with remaining olive oil, parsley, salt, and lemon wedges.

title: Tosta de Aguacate y Gambas
shortDescription: Toasted bread with avocado and garlic shrimp
note: Assemble right before serving so the toast stays crisp.
introCopy: Crisp toasted bread layered with mashed avocado and quick garlic-sizzled shrimp — a modern tapas-bar favorite.

steps.text: Toast the baguette slices until golden and crisp, about 3 minutes under the broiler.
Mash the avocado with lime juice and salt.
Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a skillet over high heat, add shrimp and garlic, and cook 2-3 minutes until pink.
Spread the mashed avocado on the toasts, top with garlic shrimp, and finish with chili flakes and remaining oil.

title: Zanahorias Aliñadas
shortDescription: Marinated carrots, cumin, garlic, sherry vinegar
note: An Andalusian tapas-bar staple, often served alongside olives.
introCopy: Cooked carrot rounds marinated in a cumin-spiked garlic vinaigrette — bright, tangy, and simple.

steps.text: Boil the carrot rounds in salted water 6-8 minutes until just tender, then drain.
Whisk together garlic, cumin, sherry vinegar, olive oil, and salt.
Toss the warm carrots with the dressing and let marinate at least 15 minutes.
Serve at room temperature or chilled.

title: Remojón Granadino
shortDescription: Orange, salt cod, and onion salad from Granada
note: A refreshing, olive-studded cousin of the orange and cod salad above — this one leans on egg and black olives.
introCopy: A Granada specialty pairing sweet oranges with salt cod, hard-boiled egg, and black olives in one bright, contrasting salad.

steps.text: Arrange the orange segments and red onion on a platter.
Scatter the flaked cod over the top, then tuck in the egg quarters and olives.
Drizzle generously with olive oil and serve at room temperature.

title: Champiñones Rellenos
shortDescription: Mushrooms stuffed with garlic, breadcrumbs, and herbs
note: Swap in goat cheese for a creamier filling if you like.
introCopy: Button mushroom caps filled with a garlicky, herby breadcrumb stuffing and roasted until golden.

steps.text: Heat oven to 400°F. Finely chop the reserved mushroom stems.
Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a skillet, cook chopped stems and garlic until soft, about 4 minutes.
Stir in breadcrumbs, parsley, salt, and pepper off heat.
Fill each mushroom cap with the stuffing, arrange on a tray, drizzle with remaining oil, and bake 15 minutes until golden.

title: Espárragos Trigueros a la Plancha
shortDescription: Griddled wild asparagus, garlic, sea salt, lemon
note: Best in spring when wild asparagus is thin and tender.
introCopy: Thin wild asparagus spears seared hard and fast until charred at the tips and tender within.

steps.text: Heat a griddle over high heat with the olive oil.
Sear the asparagus 4-5 minutes, turning occasionally, until charred in spots and just tender.
Add garlic in the last minute of cooking.
Season with flaky salt and serve with lemon wedges.

title: Pincho Moruno
shortDescription: Spiced pork skewers, cumin, paprika, coriander
note: Great with cold beer and a squeeze of lemon.
introCopy: Cubed pork marinated in a North African-inspired spice blend and grilled on skewers until charred and juicy.

steps.text: Toss the pork cubes with olive oil, garlic, cumin, paprika, coriander, and cayenne. Marinate at least 1 hour, or overnight.
Thread the pork onto skewers.
Grill or griddle over high heat 8-10 minutes, turning, until charred outside and cooked through.
Serve hot with lemon wedges.

title: Berberechos al Natural
shortDescription: Steamed cockles with lemon
note: As simple as tapas gets — let the shellfish speak for itself.
introCopy: Tiny cockles steamed just until they open, served with nothing more than lemon and their own briny liquor.

steps.text: Place cockles and water in a wide pot over high heat, cover, and steam 3-4 minutes until they open.
Discard any that stay closed. Spoon into bowls with a little of the cooking liquid.
Serve hot with lemon wedges and flaky salt.

title: Tortillitas de Camarones
shortDescription: Crisp shrimp fritters, chickpea flour, scallion
note: Blot briefly on paper towels, but serve while still crackling hot.
introCopy: Paper-thin, lacy fritters studded with tiny shrimp — a Cádiz specialty fried until shatteringly crisp.

steps.text: Whisk chickpea flour, all-purpose flour, water, and salt into a thin, pourable batter.
Stir in the shrimp, scallions, and parsley.
Heat olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Ladle in thin rounds of batter and fry 2-3 minutes per side until lacy and golden.
Drain briefly on paper towels and serve immediately.

title: Queso Manchego con Membrillo
shortDescription: Manchego cheese with quince paste
note: A five-minute tapa that never fails a crowd.
introCopy: Firm, nutty Manchego sliced alongside sweet quince paste — the classic Spanish cheese-and-fruit pairing.

steps.text: Arrange the Manchego and quince paste slices alternately on a plate.
Scatter with toasted almonds if using, and serve at room temperature.

title: Jamón con Melón
shortDescription: Cured ham draped over sweet ripe melon
note: Use a ripe, fragrant melon — it makes all the difference.
introCopy: Thin ribbons of cured ham over chilled, sweet melon — the classic salty-sweet Spanish pairing.

ingredients.prepNote: peeled, seeded, and sliced into wedges

steps.text: Chill the melon wedges until cold.
Drape a slice of ham over each melon wedge.
Finish with a crack of black pepper and serve immediately.

title: Ensalada de Judías Verdes con Almendras
shortDescription: Green beans with toasted almonds and garlic
note: Equally good warm or chilled the next day.
introCopy: Crisp-tender green beans tossed with toasted almonds, garlic, and a splash of sherry vinegar.

steps.text: Blanch the green beans in salted boiling water 4-5 minutes until crisp-tender, then drain.
Warm olive oil in a skillet and cook garlic until fragrant and just golden, about 1 minute.
Toss the green beans with the garlic oil, sherry vinegar, and toasted almonds.
Season with salt and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Vieiras a la Plancha
shortDescription: Griddled scallops, garlic, lemon, parsley
note: Pat the scallops very dry for the best sear.
introCopy: Sweet scallops seared hard for a deep golden crust, finished simply with garlic, lemon, and parsley.

steps.text: Heat olive oil in a heavy skillet over high heat until shimmering.
Sear the scallops 1.5-2 minutes per side until deeply golden and just opaque in the center.
Add garlic in the last 30 seconds, then remove from heat and squeeze over lemon juice.
Season with salt and pepper, scatter with parsley, and serve immediately.

title: Calamares a la Plancha
shortDescription: Griddled squid, garlic, olive oil, lemon
note: A lighter alternative to fried calamari, just as popular in tapas bars.
introCopy: Whole baby squid seared fast over high heat, kept tender with a short cook time, finished with garlic and lemon.

steps.text: Score the squid bodies lightly and pat very dry.
Heat a griddle over high heat with half the olive oil until smoking.
Sear the squid 1-2 minutes per side until opaque and lightly charred — don't overcook.
Toss with garlic, remaining oil, parsley, and salt. Serve with lemon wedges.

title: Rape a la Plancha con Ajada
shortDescription: Pan-seared monkfish with garlic-paprika oil
note: Ajada is the same garlic-paprika oil used on Galician octopus — equally good here.
introCopy: Firm monkfish medallions seared until golden, finished with a warm garlic and smoked paprika oil.

steps.text: Season the monkfish medallions with salt. Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear the monkfish 3-4 minutes per side until golden and just cooked through. Transfer to a plate.
In the same pan, warm remaining oil and garlic over low heat until fragrant, about 1 minute, then off heat stir in smoked paprika and sherry vinegar.
Spoon the ajada over the monkfish and serve immediately.

title: Habitas con Menta
shortDescription: Baby fava beans with mint, garlic, and olive oil
note: A springtime tapa best made when fresh fava beans are in season.
introCopy: Tender baby fava beans sautéed briefly with garlic and finished with fresh mint — light, green, and full of spring flavor.

steps.text: Blanch the fava beans in boiling salted water 2 minutes, then drain and peel the outer skins if desired.
Heat olive oil in a skillet and cook garlic until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add the favas and sauté 3-4 minutes until tender and bright green.
Off heat, stir in mint and season with salt. Serve warm.
